question:
Why: T3 (RL-75) compared ridge B5D-fc (8 aggregated weather features, learned per station) with zero-shot Chronos-2 (raw
series), so its conclusion mixes model and encoding. Its line "pure Chronos is best at <= 3 h" was only tested against B4D-n.
A post-hoc mean of Chronos none and B5D-fc looked better than both on the same 8 stations, which therefore cannot confirm it.

conf.origins: eligibility on target and forecast weather presence only; no observed-weather requirement

prior_use_of_conf_data: Temp and forecasts of 184841 were not used by T3. Paper 2 F4 used only DO/Turb of 184841. Step 0 read flags / presence only, never a forecast error.

weather.source: Open-Meteo Previous Runs best_match at WQ station coordinates (same code as T3)

chronos.train_origins: every 180 min in the train window, eligibility on presence; targets end before test start. Zero-shot, so train-year forecasts are out-of-sample by construction; the model's own training cutoff is outside this repo's control.

ridge.recipe: t3.ridge_fit_predict, per station x horizon, lambdas and selection as T3
ridge.ridge-B5D-fc: T3 recipe, 30-min training origins; dev must reproduce T3's stored forecasts to 1e-6
ridge.ridge-B5D-fc-3h: same features, 3-h training origins = training set of the trained arms
ridge.resid-none: target actual - q50, features = the 8 weather features only

verdict_rules.gate: t3.gate_nerrs unchanged (>= 4/5 equal time blocks lower MAE and RMSE, DM-HLN p < 0.05 on per-slot mean absolute loss, lag = ceil(h / 6 h)). Block windows are fixed in advance: dev ends 2025-12-31 12:00 (as T3), conf ends 2025-12-31 06:00 (last eligible origin in step 0).
verdict_rules.references: Each arm is compared with Chronos none and with ridge B5D-fc. Trained arms (resid-none, stack-B5D) use ridge-B5D-fc-3h, a B5D-fc retrained on the identical 3-h training-origin set, so that training stride is not confounded with hybridisation; avg and switch-180 use ridge-B5D-fc in the T3 recipe (30-min training origins). Trained arm vs the T3-recipe ridge and ridge-3h vs T3-recipe ridge are secondary.
verdict_rules.holm_family: conf only, 42 tests: {resid-none, stack-B5D, avg} x {none, ridge reference} x 6 horizons (36) + switch-180 x its non-degenerate reference x 6 horizons (ridge at h <= 180, none at h > 180).
verdict_rules.reserve_call: For a pair at a horizon, 'win' iff pooled gate passes AND Holm p < 0.05 AND MAE ratio < 1 in 3/3 reserves AND day-block bootstrap 95 % CI of the ratio is entirely below 1 in >= 2/3 reserves. 'loss' is the mirror image (reference passes the gate, ratio > 1 in 3/3, CI entirely above 1 in >= 2/3). Otherwise 'tie'. With 3 reserves no inferential test at reserve level exists: this is a descriptive consistency rule, and reserves are the unit of independence.
verdict_rules.arm_conclusion: An arm 'beats both' at a horizon iff its reserve_call is 'win' against both references. Label: 'supported' if >= 4/6 horizons, 'partial' if 1-3, 'not_supported' if 0. Claim 'hybrid helps at 6-12 h' needs 'beats both' at both 360 and 720 for that arm. switch-180 equals one reference at every horizon, so it is judged only against the other: same labels on reserve_call 'win' vs the non-degenerate reference.
verdict_rules.encoding_reading: Read at 360 and 720 min from resid-none vs ridge-B5D-fc-3h: if the call is 'loss' at either horizon, 'ridge advantage survives identical weather features' (the T3 gap is not only encoding); otherwise 'T3 gap at 6-12 h not attributable to the Chronos backbone given identical features'. stack-B5D contains the ridge features and is not used for this reading.
verdict_rules.station_level: Per pair x horizon, secondary, plan section 5.3: share of stations won, median MAE skill, two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank and sign test on per-station MAE differences. Stations in one reserve are not independent (apaebwq / apaeswq share one site and weather cell), so reserve_call decides, not these tests.
verdict_rules.persistence: Every model vs persistence: gate and ratio per horizon, secondary; skill = 1 - MAE / MAE persistence.
verdict_rules.dev_protocol: dev is exploratory: reported with the same tables, never used to choose an arm, threshold, feature or lambda rule. Only a coding bug found on dev may change the code, and then by a committed amendment listed in NOTES.md before conf is scored.
verdict_rules.conf_protocol: evaluate --set conf runs once into a write-once directory. Anything else on conf is labelled post-hoc in NOTES.md.
verdict_rules.negative_results: A negative or tied verdict is reported as such.

known_limits_before_scoring: Jobos: job19wq has 0 eligible origins in blocks 1-2 and job10wq 3 in block 1, so Jobos block 1 is essentially job09 + job20.
apaebwq / apaeswq are bottom and surface sondes of one site and share weather.
CDMO 2025 is provisional; same 11-month test year as T3, so dev and conf share weather events only if regional.
